**Verdict: Ready for the maintainer to merge.**

Thanks for the careful slice. Reviewed at head 19221ec, trial-merged with current `upstream/main` (clean, no conflicts).

**What looks good**
- Acquit-only design (`verify/mesh_steel.rs`): the box laws run first and the mesh can only clear a hit, never add one. Their deliberate silences and labels are untouched where nothing is cleared.
- Every unproven case is a hit: GJK gap proof with `FIXTURE_HIT_TOL` plus arc pad, ray parity with ambiguous results counted as inside, closed meshes only. Open, non-finite, empty, collapsed or over-4M meshes return a named `MeshError` and are logged (`fixture::log_mesh_refusals`).
- Scope kept narrow: tilted, C-turned and XZ/YZ-arc moves, lathe tool kinds and shared boxes keep the box verdict.
- No `unwrap`/`expect`/`panic!` in the new modules; indexing is on fixed-size arrays or internally built ids. New files all carry a provenance header and are under 400 lines (`mesh_steel.rs` 293, `gjk.rs` 284).
- Meshes are cached once per setup in `posting::fixture_findings`; the generate path and the post gate speak one verdict.
- No `build.rs`, dependency, `.github` or script changes. A decisions file is present (`docs/decisions/339-fixture-mesh.md`), and `CHANGELOG.md` is not edited.
- Body has a `Changelog:` line and `Refs #339`, correctly partial work.

**Local results (merged with main, macOS, debug)**

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| `cargo test -p camcraft-sim -p camcraft-app --no-run` | builds |
| sim `fixture_mesh` | 9 passed, 1 ignored (heavy lane) |
| app `fixture_mesh` | 3 passed |
| sim lib | 62 passed |
| app `fixtures` / `fixture_law_gaps` / `rotary_fixtures` / `carried_fixtures_cache` | 14 / 3 / 4 / 6 passed |
| sim `fixture_stack_span` / `fixture_arc_sagitta` / `posed_fixture` / `posed_fixture_midpose` | 8 / 10 / 7 / 3 passed |
| `clippy -p camcraft-sim -p camcraft-app --all-targets -D warnings` | clean |

The ignored 200k-facet timing lane and the other app suites were not run; the PR notes `setup_stock_source` is red on main (#415).

**Requested before merge**
None.

**Questions / notes (not blocking)**
- `crates/app/src/operation/generate.rs` is 3203 lines and grows by about 20; already far over the 400-line guide, so the next change there is a good moment to split.
- The body says "Fixes"-free `Refs #339` and the commit subjects are conventional; the branch carries three merge commits from `upstream/main`, which is fine for a merge-commit repo.
- A `feat`, so it waits for the minor cut.

A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.

<!-- pr-reviewer: 19221ecc7b03da8ab8512c4199c51a79c32550dd -->
**Verdict: Ready for the maintainer to merge.**

Reviewed at head 19221ec, trial-merged with current `origin/main` (clean). Note: the earlier comment carrying this marker was posted from the PR author's own account, not by the project reviewer; this is the independent review.

**What looks good**
- Acquit-only: `mesh_refined` runs the box law first and the mesh can only drop a hit a flagging box made (`verify/mesh_steel.rs`). Unjudged cases (posed, C-turned, XZ/YZ arcs, shared boxes, open/refused meshes, lathe tools) keep the box verdict. A move survives if any flagging box is kept or unjudged.
- GJK proof is sound for any search state: `separated` returns true only when `v.w > margin*|v|` with `w` the exact support of A-B along `-v` (`gjk.rs`), independent of simplex arithmetic. A capped (48 iters), non-finite or overlapping search answers "hit". The swept band is the exact convex Minkowski sum, so its support is exact.
- BVH pruning is inflated: node boxes are tested with `margin = FIXTURE_HIT_TOL + arc pad + 1e-9*scale`, and a node is pruned only by the same GJK proof against its box (a superset of its triangles).
- Point-in-solid: six fixed off-axis rays, any edge/vertex/graze/on-surface crossing discards the ray, all ambiguous reads as inside; inside on nonzero winding or odd parity. Closed-mesh check is signed per-edge, so a flipped or cracked mesh is `MeshError::Open` and keeps the box.
- Whole stack judged: shank, every `HolderStack` band (#381), spindle housing when stated, flute, on feeds and rapids alike; non-numeric band means hit. Arc chords are padded by their sagitta plus 1 um; ramps are swept at true z (the sloped chord), not the lowest z.
- #424 and #425: both are already closed on main (`stack_span`, merged before this PR). This PR leaves those box laws untouched and does not worsen them. Because the mesh only acquits, it also cannot cover a box-law miss; the mesh judges the whole stack along true z, so it never acquits a ramp or rapid the box convicts on stack grounds unless the steel is genuinely clear.
- No `unwrap`/`expect`/`panic!` in the new modules; index math is on internally built ids with `.get` at the query boundaries; non-finite input is refused by name (`MeshError`) and logged. New files are 119 to 293 lines with provenance headers citing GJK (1988), van den Bergen (1999), Ericson, Moller-Trumbore. No dependency, build.rs, script or `.github` changes; no CHANGELOG or snapshot PNG edits in the PR; decisions file present.

**Local results (merged with main, Windows, debug)**

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| sim `--test fixture_mesh` | 9 passed, 1 ignored (200k-facet heavy lane) |
| sim lib | 62 passed |
| app `fixture_mesh` / `fixtures` / `carried_fixtures_cache` / `posting` | 3 / 14 / 6 / 17 passed |
| `clippy -p camcraft-sim -p camcraft-app --all-targets -D warnings` | clean |

**Requested before merge**
None.

**Notes (not blocking)**
1. The acquit margin is `FIXTURE_HIT_TOL` (1 nm) plus a float-dust pad, the same tolerance the box laws use. A path 1 um from a jaw now posts clean where the box refused. Correct as geometry, but consider a user-visible safety clearance in slice 2 (the issue's later slices).
2. Tests cover the vise cases well but there is no randomized cross-check of the mesh verdict against a brute-force triangle-distance oracle, nor an arc-chord case in the sim suite (arcs are only in the app test). Worth adding when slice 2 lets the mesh add hits.
3. `generate.rs` is far over the 400-line guide (grows about 20 lines); not blocking.
4. A `feat`: waits for the minor cut.

A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.
